title: fix: move Pruna image models to DeepInfra
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Routes `p-image` and `p-image-edit` through the exact DeepInfra Pruna endpoints.
- Preserves canonical names, aliases, parameters, paid-only access, multiplier 1, and `$0.005`/`$0.01` image prices.
- Keeps `p-video-720p` and `p-video-1080p` unchanged on Replicate pending canonical resolution-aware billing.
- Adds focused route tests; full Gen suite passes 752/752 and both workers type-check.
- Paid local E2E passed generation, JPEG/PNG editing, five references, every alias, validation, media inspection, and exact `$0.015` combined wallet deduction.

No fallback, GPU deployment, or secret mutation.

gist.headline: Pruna found a new greenhouse
gist.blurb: The Pruna image models have moved their rendering nest to DeepInfra without changing the names, knobs, or prices anyone already knows. Image generation and editing keep buzzing along, now through the exact provider routes.
gist.summary: Routed `p-image` and `p-image-edit` to DeepInfra's Pruna endpoints while preserving canonical names, aliases, parameters, paid-only access, multiplier 1, and $0.005/$0.01 image pricing; Pruna video models remain on Replicate.
gist.impact: Paid users can continue generating and editing Pruna images through every existing alias, including JPEG/PNG edits and up to five references, with the same validated behavior and exact wallet deductions.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Polli carefully moving two labeled Pruna image jars from an old Replicate garden shed to a cozy DeepInfra greenhouse, with a retro terminal confirming that image and edit routes still preserve their familiar labels and prices. Show thriving code-plants, five small reference-photo frames, and a tiny receipt reading "$0.015" to represent tested multi-step billing continuity.
